title: Short-circuit guards and exclusive or

blocks.text: `&&` and `||` **short-circuit**: when the left operand already decides the answer, the right one is never evaluated. That is what makes a guard like `s != null && s.length() > 0` safe. The non-short-circuit `&` and `|` evaluate both sides every time. On booleans, `^` is true when the operands differ.

items: `startsWithDigit(String text)` returns whether the first character of `text` is a digit. `null` and the empty string return `false` and never throw.
`exactlyOne(boolean a, boolean b)` returns `true` when exactly one of the two is `true`.

cases.says: Both methods answer for ordinary inputs.
null text returns false instead of throwing.
Empty text returns false: the guard stops before charAt(0) is ever evaluated.

concepts: On booleans, ^ is true when the operands differ.
&& and || short-circuit, while & and | evaluate both operands.
